title: Java Programming
description: Beginner-to-advanced Java reference covering the type system, object model, collections, streams, exceptions, generics, records, sealed types, concurrency, JVM behavior, testing, and production practices.

sections.title: Syntax, Types & Control Flow
sections.description: Understand Java's static type system, value/reference semantics, null boundary, and expression-oriented modern syntax.

subtopics.title: Primitives, References & null
subtopics.description: Primitive variables contain values; reference variables identify objects. Java always passes arguments by value—even when the copied value is an object reference.

table.title: Primitive and Reference Semantics
rows: Use policy for NaN and precision

callouts.title: No Nullable Type in Core Java
callouts.text: Treat nullability as an API contract. Validate at boundaries, avoid returning null collections, and use Optional mainly for return values—not fields or parameters by default.

subtopics.title: Control Flow, switch & Pattern Matching
subtopics.description: Modern switch can return a value and use exhaustive type patterns. Guard clauses keep failure paths explicit.

callouts.title: Exhaustiveness Is a Design Tool
callouts.text: Sealed hierarchies plus switch make missing domain cases compiler-visible. Keep the permitted set close to the abstraction.

subtopics.title: Strings, Numbers & Time
subtopics.description: String is immutable; BigDecimal is for explicit decimal precision; java.time types separate instants, local civil time, zones, and durations.

callouts.title: Do Not Construct BigDecimal from double
callouts.text: Use a decimal string or BigDecimal.valueOf. Define scale and RoundingMode at the domain boundary.

subtopics.title: Classes, Interfaces & Composition
subtopics.description: Keep invariants inside constructors/factories, expose behavior rather than mutable internals, and prefer composition over inheritance for replaceable policy.

callouts.title: Defensive Ownership
callouts.text: Copy mutable inputs and return unmodifiable snapshots when callers must not mutate internal state.

subtopics.title: Records, Sealed Types & Enums
subtopics.description: Records model transparent data aggregates; sealed types bound polymorphic families; enums represent a fixed set with identity and behavior.

callouts.title: Records Are Shallowly Immutable
callouts.text: Record components are final references, but referenced collections or objects may still mutate. Copy them in the compact constructor.

subtopics.title: Generics, Bounds & PECS
subtopics.description: Generics provide compile-time type safety with erasure. Use ? extends T for producers and ? super T for consumers.

callouts.title: Generic Types Are Invariant
callouts.text: List<Integer> is not a subtype of List<Number>. Wildcards express safe read/write variance at API boundaries.

subtopics.title: List, Set, Map & Queues
subtopics.description: Program to collection interfaces and choose implementations by ordering, uniqueness, lookup, concurrency, and mutation requirements.

subtopics.title: Streams, Collectors & Parallelism
subtopics.description: Streams are single-use lazy pipelines. Keep operations stateless and non-interfering; collect explicitly at the boundary.

callouts.title: parallelStream Is Not a Free Speedup
callouts.text: Measure workload size, splitting cost, ordering, blocking, and common-pool contention. Prefer explicit executors for controlled services.

subtopics.title: Exceptions & Resource Ownership
subtopics.description: Use checked exceptions only when callers can recover meaningfully; preserve causes; close resources with try-with-resources.

callouts.title: Do Not Swallow Interruption
callouts.text: If InterruptedException cannot be propagated, restore the flag with Thread.currentThread().interrupt() and stop the operation.

subtopics.title: Virtual Threads, Executors & Futures
subtopics.description: Virtual threads make thread-per-task practical for blocking I/O; platform pools remain suitable for bounded CPU work. Structured ownership still matters.

callouts.title: Virtual Threads Do Not Make CPU Work Parallel for Free
callouts.text: They improve blocking concurrency, not compute throughput. Bound scarce downstream resources and avoid pinning through long blocking synchronized sections.

subtopics.title: Memory, GC & Observability
subtopics.description: Diagnose allocation rate, retained objects, GC pauses, thread states, and latency together. Use JFR, thread dumps, heap dumps, and metrics before tuning flags.

codeBlocks.code:
jcmd <pid> JFR.start name=profile duration=60s filename=app.jfr
jcmd <pid> Thread.print
jcmd <pid> GC.heap_info

callouts.title: Measure Before Tuning
callouts.text: Most memory incidents are ownership, cache, or allocation problems. GC flags cannot repair unbounded retention.

subtopics.title: Testing, Build & Review Checklist
subtopics.description: Use focused unit tests, integration tests for real boundaries, reproducible builds, static analysis, dependency locking, and graceful shutdown checks.

callouts.title: Production Checklist
callouts.text: Pin the JDK toolchain, avoid mutable globals, bound concurrency and queues, configure timeouts, preserve causes, redact secrets, expose health/metrics, and test shutdown.
